R221.note: ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync parameterizes AccountId/Status/BeforeUtc via FormattableString, closing injection while preserving the Task<int> row-count contract.

R222.note: %15s bounds the write and closes the overflow, but per the stated contract an over-length token must be rejected (-1), not silently truncated and accepted; write-up doesn't mention or handle this.

R223.note: res.sendFile(requestedFile, {root}) is Express's own containment mechanism; unused reportPath correctly removed, legitimate downloads unaffected.

R224.note: Standard HTML-entity escaping applied only to the untrusted closingNote; other interpolations unaffected.

R225.note: ValidAlgorithms pins RS256, blocking HS256 algorithm-confusion; only that property is added, throw-on-failure contract unchanged.

R226.note: offset + length > capacity is the right shape but offset/length are size_t and can overflow/wrap, letting a crafted huge offset bypass the check and still overrun the buffer; unaddressed.

R227.note: Denylist of method-name identifiers is a weak boundary for compiled/executed arbitrary code (e.g. plural GetMethods/GetProperties aren't blocked, only singular forms) so the vector isn't reliably closed; namespace allowlist restriction is at least disclosed.

R228.note: Inserting the '--' end-of-options marker before filenames matches the stated contract exactly and preserves normal archiving.

R229.note: crypto/rand.Read correctly replaces the weak PRNG, but the output becomes a 64-char hex string instead of the contract's 32-character same-alphabet key; change is openly stated in the write-up, not silent.

R230.note: Path / operator has the same absolute-path override issue as os.path.join, but the subsequent is_relative_to(BASE_DIR) check catches it and rejects with 403; legitimate files still served and 404 preserved.

R231.note: shared_ptr captured by value keeps the Session alive for the queued callback, matching the contract's 'own/share' branch; signature change is shown plainly in the diff.

R232.note: Argument array removes shell metacharacter injection, but a leading '-' in inputPath/outputPath can still be read as an ImageMagick option/coder (option-injection gap), which isn't addressed.

R233.note: Extension is now derived solely from the already-validated detected content type via a 1:1 map with allowedContentTypes; no functional change for legitimate uploads.

R234.note: Removing mark_safe() and rendering with plain {{ announcement }} closes the XSS but also escapes the intended <div> wrapper markup the function still bakes in, breaking the banner's HTML rendering; not disclosed.

R235.note: resolve_entities=False/load_dtd=False/no_network=True is the standard lxml XXE closure; well-formed XML without external entities parses unchanged.

R236.note: PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder correctly parameterizes customerId; found/not-found output paths preserved.

R237.note: SHA256 allowlist is an appropriate integrity gate given no .NET Core sandboxing, but it turns the 'upload a new plugin at runtime' endpoint into 'upload only pre-approved binaries' - a real capability loss, though the write-up states this openly.

R238.note: Key($publicKey,'RS256') pins one algorithm, the correct 6.x+ fix for the HS256/RS256 confusion; the HS256 branch was already non-functional for legitimate tokens (always used $publicKey, never $hmacSecret), so dropping it doesn't remove working behavior.
